chosen.premise: Spearow’s warning cry carries over half a mile, turning one tiny bird into a long-range danger alarm.
chosen.hook: This tiny bird can warn Pokémon over half a mile away.
chosen.visualIdea: A tiny Spearow cries from a field as a soundwave ring expands past a half-mile marker and alerts distant Spearow.
chosen.note: The half-mile figure is a strong, concrete hook directly supported by Ruby and Emerald entries. The tiny size makes the range more striking, and soundwave visualization is immediate.

candidates.premise: Spearow can’t fly high or far, yet its short wings let it dart at high speed to defend territory.
candidates.hook: Spearow is bad at flying—until you enter its territory.
candidates.visualIdea: Split screen: Spearow fails to climb high, then instantly zigzags around a territory boundary at high speed.
candidates.note: A strong built-in contradiction: poor at height and long distance, but fast around its territory. Multiple entries directly support both halves, though fast defensive movement is a familiar bird-Pokémon framing.

candidates.premise: Spearow pecks Bug-type Pokémon in tall grass so effectively that farmers look after it when pests trouble fields.
candidates.hook: Farmers protect Spearow because it eats their bug problem.
candidates.visualIdea: A field fills with bug Pokémon; Spearow flushes them from grass, pecks them, then receives food from relieved farmers.
candidates.note: The farmer relationship is a memorable ecological detail, directly supported by Moon and reinforced by its grass-foraging entries. It is slightly broader than a single measurable fact, but makes an excellent mini-story.

candidates.premise: Despite being only 0.3 meters tall and 2 kilograms, Spearow will confront even large Pokémon over territory.
candidates.hook: This 2-kilogram bird will pick a fight with giants.
candidates.visualIdea: A scale graphic dwarfs tiny Spearow beside a huge silhouette, then Spearow charges across a territorial boundary.
candidates.note: The 0.3 m, 2 kg versus large-Pokémon contrast is immediately legible and well supported by Ultra Sun. It overlaps with the fast territorial-defense angle, but has a stronger character-based visual.

candidates.premise: Spearow’s short wings are so limiting that it must flap rapidly just to stay airborne.
candidates.hook: Spearow has to work this hard just to stay in the air.
candidates.visualIdea: Close-up of tiny wings beating like a rapid fan, with a hovering meter showing constant effort to remain airborne.
candidates.note: Well-supported and highly animatable, especially the rapid wingbeat concept. But 'small wings flap fast' is less distinctive than Spearow's territorial behavior or half-mile cry.

candidates.premise: At level 20, the tiny bird Spearow evolves into Fearow while keeping its Normal/Flying typing.
candidates.hook: At level 20, Spearow becomes Fearow—without changing type.
candidates.visualIdea: A level counter climbs to 20; Spearow flashes into Fearow while Normal and Flying type badges remain fixed onscreen.
candidates.note: Accurate and concrete, but a standard evolution fact with little Spearow-specific insight. Keeping the same typing is common and not especially surprising.

rounds.request: None needed. The half-mile alarm is strong enough: it has a precise number, a surprising scale contrast with Spearow's 0.3 m / 2 kg body, direct official-entry support, and a clear soundwave visual.
